subject: microbiology
title: Salmonella: enteric fever and non typhoidal disease

steps.tx: **Enteric fever** (Typhi and Paratyphi A, B, C) starts with step ladder fever climbing over week one with headache, then **rose spots** (faint truncal macules), splenomegaly and **relative bradycardia** (Faget sign: pulse lagging temperature) in week two. Bacteria invade ileal **Peyer patches**, and week three threatens **perforation with peritonitis** or gastrointestinal bleeding. Paratyphi runs milder; **Vi capsule** shields Typhi from complement. Humans are the only reservoir, spread by the 5 Fs with contaminated water.
steps.say: Step ladder fever plus rose spots plus slow pulse is enteric fever. Week three perforates ileum.

vis.alt: Timeline diagram showing the clinical progression of enteric fever over three weeks, including fever, headache, rose spots, splenomegaly, Peyer patch invasion, and perforation.
vis.caption: Enteric fever: Clinical course and complications

steps.tx: **Chronic carriers** (2 to 5 percent, gallbladder colonisation especially with gallstones, shedding Vi positive bacilli in stool) sustain endemicity; food handlers need exclusion with clearance cultures. Complications beyond perforation include encephalopathy (muttering delirium, typhoid state), hepatitis, pneumonia, myocarditis and osteomyelitis. Relapse follows inadequate therapy as intracellular bacilli resurge. Paratyphi B (Schottmuller) and C add focal suppurations.
steps.say: Gallbladder carriers shedding Vi bacilli keep typhoid endemic. Muttering delirium with fever is typhoid state.

steps.tx: **Diagnosis follows the week**: week one **blood culture** (highest yield before antibiotics), week two stool culture with rising **Widal O and H titres** (O appears first, H persists; single titres mislead in endemic zones, paired rising titres diagnose), week three urine culture. **Bone marrow culture** stays most sensitive even after antibiotics (intracellular niche). TyphiDot IgM and IDL Tubex support rapid calls; **leukopenia with eosinopenia** (rather than leukocytosis) hints enteric over other fevers. Vi serology flags carriers.
steps.say: Bleed cultures week one, Widal rising week two, marrow beats all. Leukopenia points to typhoid.

steps.tx: **Treatment** outruns resistance: **ceftriaxone or azithromycin** for MDR strains (chloramphenicol, ampicillin and cotrimoxazole resistance), with **fluoroquinolone resistance** (gyrA mutations, nalidixic acid screen) now widespread in South Asia forcing XDR regimens (azithromycin plus meropenem debates). Carriers get prolonged ciprofloxacin with **cholecystectomy** when stones persist. Vaccines: **Ty21a oral live** (3 year cover) versus **Vi polysaccharide injectable** (single dose, no memory, over 2 years) versus Vi conjugate (Typbar TCV, infants, memory). Sanitation prevents; vaccines bridge.
steps.say: MDR typhoid gets ceftriaxone or azithromycin. Vi conjugate protects infants with memory.
